title: Agent Flight Recorder
subtitle: From an agent's answer to evidence you can inspect.

lines: An AI agent says, done.
But what happened? And does the evidence still support the result?
Maya's coding agent runs a test, changes the code, then announces: ready to ship.
But that passing test checked the old code.
Agent Flight Recorder is a black box for agent execution.
Prompts, tools, errors, retries, and policies become one ordered story.
Maya rewinds to the moment things changed.
She inspects each step and its recorded state, without running the tools again.
An external-recipient action pauses for review. Restricted reads are blocked.
In this demo, approval creates a local receipt, not a real email.
Insights link failures, retries, and delays to their source runs.
Maya investigates causes, not just statuses.
Evidence Lens links each claim to its result, code version, and target.
Supported. Contradicted. Unsupported. Or unverifiable, like Maya's outdated test.
The manifest separates what was available from what was used.
Handoffs link proof, gaps, and next checks.
Maya approves a bounded demo recovery.
A fresh check creates a linked, supported run. The original stays unchanged.
Connect your agent through the SDK or HTTP.
Export recordings, or inspect them through read-only MCP.
Optional Azure drafts handoffs after approval. It never decides verdicts.
The V S Code companion encrypts local records. Private agent internals stay outside capture.
Now Maya hands over evidence, not a promise.
Agent Flight Recorder. Follow the run. Question the claim. Leave better evidence.
